title: Scaffold-free 3D cell culture of primary skin fibroblasts induces profound changes of the matrisome
projectDescription: We analyze the effect of magnetic 3D bioprinting using NanoShuttle-PL on the proteome of primary human skin fibroblasts and epidermal squamous cell carcinoma cells. NanoStuttle-PL employs magnetic nanoparticles that interact electrostatically with cells rendering them magnetic and allowing manipulation of their 3D assembly using external magnetic forces.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Cells were SILAC labeled and kept in 2D and 3D. SILAC samples were combined, proteins eluted in SDS loading buffer and separated by SDS-PAGE. Proteins were in-gel digested with trypsin, peptides purified and analyzed by LC-MS/MS.
dataProcessingProtocol: Peak detection and relative quantification of SILAC-pairs was conducted by MaxQuant versión 1.6.2.10. Peaks were searched against a full-length human Uniprot database from March 2016. Enzyme specificity was assigned to trypsin/P and quantitation was based on three SILAC labels. Carbamidomethylation was set as a fixed modification; N-terminal acetylation and oxidation of methionine. A maximum of three missed cleavages was allowed. Proteins were identified with a minimum of one unique peptide. For quantification, a ratio count of two was needed.
